relations.to: continued residual physical-security risk around Hormuz

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Hormuz shipping traffic falls below recent average
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports seven commodity-vessel transits on Thursday, down from 17 Wednesday and below the recent 10-day average, using commercial vessel-tracking data.

supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: diplomacy intensifies around conditional Hormuz reopening
supportingEvidence.note: Diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait are intensifying while Iran prepares conditions and an Iran-Oman corridor remains under discussion, creating a useful contrast with still-weak physical traffic.

supportingEvidence.title: IMO: attacks keep maritime-security risk elevated
supportingEvidence.note: IMO's primary safety statements document repeated attacks and continuing danger to commercial shipping in and around the Strait, supporting the residual-security-risk interpretation independently of market commentary.

contradictingEvidence.title: Diplomatic reopening efforts are intensifying
contradictingEvidence.note: A one-day traffic drop can be noisy and does not prove reopening has failed. Mediation, corridor planning, demining and conditionality negotiations remain active.

contradictingEvidence.title: AIS and daily transit counts are imperfect
contradictingEvidence.note: Commercial vessel-tracking data can miss dark or misclassified traffic, and a single-day decline can reverse quickly; treat this as a momentum warning, not a structural-collapse call.

falsifier: Downgrade the momentum-reversal interpretation if the next several days show sustained vessel and oil-flow recovery toward pre-conflict norms, maritime incidents subside, and freight/war-risk insurance and downstream Asian arrivals normalize. Treat this event as noise if the 7-transit day is immediately followed by durable recovery and adds no forecasting value beyond the existing diplomacy-plus-price baseline.
title: Hormuz traffic momentum reverses sharply while reopening diplomacy intensifies
summary: Visible commodity-vessel traffic through Hormuz fell to seven transits Thursday from 17 Wednesday and remained below the recent average even as diplomatic work on conditional reopening intensified. This does not prove the reopening process failed; it strengthens the existing narrative-versus-physical-state divergence and argues against declaring normalization from diplomacy or one strong traffic day.
delta: Supersede POSITIVE_TRAFFIC_MOMENTUM as the current short-term physical-flow label with MOMENTUM_REVERSAL_SIGNAL + SEVERE_RESIDUAL_IMPAIRMENT, while preserving CONDITIONAL_REOPENING_DEMANDS + MEDIATION_ACTIVE + FRAMEWORK_UNRESOLVED as the diplomatic state. Do not reinterpret one day as a structural reversal.
firstOrderImpacts: reduce confidence that the recent improvement in visible vessel traffic represented durable normalization
keep freight, war-risk insurance and Gulf-delivery risk elevated despite diplomatic optimism
increase the value of multi-day physical-flow confirmation before changing the operational state
secondOrderImpacts: Orbital Insight should separate absolute baseline, daily momentum and diplomatic state instead of collapsing them into one reopening score
Alternative-Data Alpha Hunter can test whether vessel-flow reversals plus incident telemetry lead crude, freight or insurance repricing
downstream destination arrivals remain a stronger confirmation layer than source-side political claims alone
